## Summary

Makes `entire explain --generate` surface actionable error messages when the
Claude CLI fails, instead of generic "failed to parse summary JSON" output
or silent empty errors.

## Problem

The Claude CLI returns most operational errors (auth, rate limit, invalid
model) at **exit 0** with `is_error: true` in its JSON envelope. The prior
implementation didn't check `is_error`, tried to JSON-parse the error text
as a `Summary`, and exposed users to messages like:

- `failed to parse summary JSON: ... (response: There's an issue with the selected model...)`
- `failed to generate summary: failed to generate summary: claude CLI failed (exit -1):` (double-wrapped)

For CLI crashes with no output (OOM, SIGKILL) users saw literally `Claude failed to generate the summary:` — nothing after the colon.

## What changed

**Typed error classification.** Introduces `*claudecode.ClaudeError` with a `Kind` discriminator (`auth` / `rate_limit` / `config` / `cli_missing` / `unknown`) populated from HTTP status or stderr fallback:

- 401/403 → auth, 429 → rate limit, other 4xx → config
- Envelope with auth phrasing but no status → also classified as auth (handles older CLI builds that omit `api_error_status`)
- Envelope with `is_error:true` + `result:null` → preserved with its HTTP status instead of discarded as a parse error
- Binary not on PATH → `cli_missing`
- Structured errors survive `errors.As` all the way from `claudecode.GenerateText` → `summarize.Generate` → explain

**User-facing message mapping.** `formatCheckpointSummaryError` turns each Kind into an actionable message with remediation:

| Kind | User sees |
|---|---|
| Auth | `Claude authentication failed: <detail>` + `` Run `claude login` and retry `` |
| Rate limit | `Claude rejected the summary request due to rate limits or quota: <detail>` + `Wait and retry` |
| Config | `Claude rejected the summary request: <detail>` + `Check your Claude CLI config and selected model` |
| CLI missing | `Claude CLI is not installed or not on PATH` |
| Timeout | 3-cause diagnostic (transcript size / network / API status) |
| Unknown with no message | Falls back to HTTP status or exit code so output is never empty |

**Settings groundwork.** Adds `summary_timeout_seconds` field and `SummaryTimeoutValue()` accessor. The field is not yet consumed by the generate path; the stacked follow-up PR wires it into TTY-gated deadline selection.

## Scope

All behavior changes are contained to:

- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/` — typed error + classifier + envelope parser enrichment
- `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/` — drops duplicate `fmt.Errorf` wrapping so `errors.As` survives the layer boundary (pinned by regression tests)
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go` — typed-error mapping for user output
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/` — new field + accessor

Merged with main to resolve conflicts with PR #887 (summary provider) and PR #953 (remote metadata fetch). `GenerateText` intentionally runs the subprocess directly instead of through `agent.RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI` — the shared helper collapses stderr/exit into a string, but Claude's envelope-based semantics need structured access to all three.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run check` (fmt + lint + unit + integration + e2e canary)
- [x] End-to-end simulation of 9 failure modes (auth / rate-limit / config / null-result envelope / no-status auth / stderr-only auth / OOM / CLI-missing / deadline) — every path produces a non-empty, actionable message
- [ ] Manual: `entire explain -c <id> --generate` with invalid model
- [ ] Manual: `entire explain -c <id> --generate` with claude logged out

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the subprocess execution and error-handling path for Claude-based summary generation, which could alter behavior across timeout/cancel and CLI failure modes. Well-covered by new unit tests, but still impacts a user-facing critical workflow (`explain --generate`).
> 
> **Overview**
> `entire explain --generate` now preserves and classifies Claude CLI failures into a typed `*claudecode.ClaudeError` (auth/rate-limit/config/CLI-missing/unknown) instead of flattening them into generic parse/exec errors.
> 
> Claude Code text generation now runs the `claude` subprocess directly to capture stdout/stderr/exit code, parses enriched JSON envelopes (including `is_error:true` and `result:null`), and maps structured failures to user-facing remediation messages; summary-generation layers stop re-wrapping errors so `errors.As` can detect the typed error at the explain layer.
> 
> Settings add a new `summary_timeout_seconds` field plus `SummaryTimeoutValue()` accessor (not yet wired into the generate path), and tests are expanded to cover envelope parsing, error classification, timeout/cancel behavior, and non-empty diagnostics.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 0bc148e0ad266ad7d4f833e83d02a2c77353f471. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

15	// GenerateText sends a prompt to the Claude CLI and returns the raw text response.
16	// Implements the agent.TextGenerator interface.
17	// The model parameter hints which model to use (e.g., "haiku", "sonnet").
18	// If empty, defaults to "haiku" for fast, cheap generation.
19	//
20	// Unlike most agents, this implementation runs the subprocess directly rather
21	// than through agent.RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI. The shared helper collapses
22	// stderr + exit code into a single formatted error string, but Claude CLI
23	// returns operational errors (auth, rate limit, invalid model) as exit 0
24	// with is_error:true in the JSON envelope on stdout — so we need structured
25	// access to stdout, stderr and the exit code to produce the typed ClaudeError
26	// values that formatCheckpointSummaryError maps to actionable messages.
27	func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) GenerateText(ctx context.Context, prompt string, model string) (string, error) {
28		claudePath := "claude"
29		if model == "" {
30			model = "haiku"
31		}
32	
33		commandRunner := c.CommandRunner
34		if commandRunner == nil {
35			commandRunner = exec.CommandContext
36		}
37	
38		cmd := commandRunner(ctx, claudePath,
39			"--print", "--output-format", "json",
40			"--model", model, "--setting-sources", "")
41	
42		// Isolate from the user's git repo to prevent recursive hook triggers
43		// and index pollution (matches agent.RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI behavior).
44		cmd.Dir = os.TempDir()
45		cmd.Env = agent.StripGitEnv(os.Environ())
46		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(prompt)
47	
48		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
49		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
50		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
51	
52		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
53			// Prefer a structured Claude error over bare ctx sentinels: if the CLI
54			// already emitted an is_error envelope on stdout, surface that even when
55			// the context happens to be done. Otherwise the user loses actionable
56			// auth/rate-limit/config diagnostics whenever ctx and the subprocess
57			// both fail at roughly the same time.
58			if _, env, parseErr := parseGenerateTextResponse(stdout.Bytes()); parseErr == nil && env != nil && env.IsError {
59				result := ""
60				if env.Result != nil {
61					result = *env.Result
62				}
63				exitCode := 0
64				var exitErr *exec.ExitError
65				if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
66					exitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
67				}
68				return "", classifyEnvelopeError(result, env.APIErrorStatus, exitCode)
69			}
70			// No structured signal on stdout — ctx cancellation is next most
71			// informative, since the rest is a guess.
72			if errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
73				return "", context.DeadlineExceeded
74			}
75			if errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.Canceled) {
76				return "", context.Canceled
77			}
78			if isExecNotFound(err) {
79				return "", &ClaudeError{Kind: ClaudeErrorCLIMissing, Cause: err}
80			}
81			exitCode := -1
82			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
83			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
84				exitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
85			}
86			return "", classifyStderrError(stderr.String(), exitCode)
87		}
88	
89		// Exit 0: parse the response and check for is_error (Claude CLI returns
90		// most operational errors as exit 0 with is_error:true in the envelope).
91		result, env, err := parseGenerateTextResponse(stdout.Bytes())
92		if err != nil {
93			return "", &ClaudeError{Kind: ClaudeErrorUnknown, Message: fmt.Sprintf("failed to parse claude CLI response: %v", err), Cause: err}
94		}
95		if env != nil && env.IsError {
96			return "", classifyEnvelopeError(result, env.APIErrorStatus, 0)
97		}
98	
99		return result, nil
100	}

102	// isExecNotFound returns true only when err indicates the binary was not
103	// found on PATH or at the given absolute path. It intentionally excludes
104	// other *exec.Error causes (permission denied, invalid executable format),
105	// which should surface as a generic failure so operators aren't misdirected
106	// to a reinstall when the real problem is a broken/inaccessible binary.
107	func isExecNotFound(err error) bool {
108		var execErr *exec.Error
109		if errors.As(err, &execErr) && errors.Is(execErr.Err, exec.ErrNotFound) {
110			return true
111		}
112		return errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound) || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist)
113	}

559	// generateCheckpointAISummary returns the generated summary, the effective
560	// deadline applied to the underlying call (which may be shorter than
561	// checkpointSummaryTimeout if the parent context had an earlier deadline),
562	// and any error. The effective deadline is returned so the caller can render
563	// the true timeout value in user-facing error messages instead of always
564	// showing the package default.
565	func generateCheckpointAISummary(ctx context.Context, scopedTranscript []byte, filesTouched []string, agentType types.AgentType, generator summarize.Generator) (*checkpoint.Summary, time.Duration, error) {
566		timeoutCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointSummaryTimeout)
567		timeoutDuration := checkpointSummaryTimeout
568		if deadline, ok := timeoutCtx.Deadline(); ok {
569			timeoutDuration = time.Until(deadline)
570		}
571		defer cancel()
572	
573		// scopedTranscript is read from checkpoint storage, which redacts on write.
574		summary, err := generateTranscriptSummary(timeoutCtx, redact.AlreadyRedacted(scopedTranscript), filesTouched, agentType, generator)
575		if err != nil {
576			// Only classify as ctx cancel/deadline when the error chain actually
577			// contains the sentinel. Relying on timeoutCtx.Err() here loses typed
578			// errors (e.g. *ClaudeError) when the subprocess returned a real
579			// structured failure while timeoutCtx.Err() is non-nil for any reason
580			// (parent cancelled, deadline already elapsed, etc.).
581			if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
582				return nil, timeoutDuration, fmt.Errorf("summary generation canceled: %w", err)
583			}
584			if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
585				return nil, timeoutDuration, fmt.Errorf("summary generation timed out after %s: %w", formatSummaryTimeout(timeoutDuration), err)
586			}
587			return nil, timeoutDuration, err
588		}
589	
590		return summary, timeoutDuration, nil
591	}

593	// formatCheckpointSummaryError maps typed Claude CLI errors and context
594	// sentinels to user-facing messages.
595	func formatCheckpointSummaryError(err error, deadline time.Duration) error {
596		var claudeErr *claudecode.ClaudeError
597		switch {
598		case errors.As(err, &claudeErr):
599			switch claudeErr.Kind { //nolint:exhaustive // ClaudeErrorUnknown handled by default
600			case claudecode.ClaudeErrorAuth:
601				return fmt.Errorf("Claude authentication failed%s\nRun `claude login` and retry", formatMessageSuffix(claudeErr.Message)) //nolint:staticcheck // ST1005: capitalized because Claude is a proper noun
602			case claudecode.ClaudeErrorRateLimit:
603				return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request due to rate limits or quota%s\nWait and retry", formatMessageSuffix(claudeErr.Message)) //nolint:staticcheck // ST1005
604			case claudecode.ClaudeErrorConfig:
605				return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request%s\nCheck your Claude CLI config and selected model", formatMessageSuffix(claudeErr.Message)) //nolint:staticcheck // ST1005
606			case claudecode.ClaudeErrorCLIMissing:
607				return errors.New("Claude CLI is not installed or not on PATH") //nolint:staticcheck // ST1005
608			default:
609				return fmt.Errorf("Claude failed to generate the summary%s", formatClaudeErrorSuffix(claudeErr)) //nolint:staticcheck // ST1005
610			}
611		case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
612			// Deliberately provider-neutral: explain --generate supports multiple
613			// summary providers (claude-code, codex, gemini, ...), so hardcoding
614			// "Claude" / "sonnet" / "Anthropic" here would misdirect users who
615			// selected a different provider in .entire/settings.json.
616			return fmt.Errorf(
617				"summary generation did not return within the %s safety deadline. This usually means one of:\n"+
618					"  - the selected model is taking longer than expected on a large transcript\n"+
619					"  - the summary provider's CLI cannot reach its API (network, VPN, firewall)\n"+
620					"    Try: run the provider CLI directly to confirm it works\n"+
621					"  - the provider's API is degraded",
622				formatSummaryTimeout(deadline))
623		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
624			return errors.New("summary generation canceled")
625		default:
626			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate summary: %w", err)
627		}
628	}

630	// formatMessageSuffix formats ": <msg>" when msg is non-empty and "" otherwise.
631	// Used by the Auth / RateLimit / Config branches of formatCheckpointSummaryError
632	// to avoid rendering a bare colon when ClaudeError.Message is empty (reachable
633	// when the CLI envelope is is_error:true with result:null but a real status).
634	func formatMessageSuffix(msg string) string {
635		if msg == "" {
636			return ""
637		}
638		return ": " + msg
639	}
640	
641	// formatClaudeErrorSuffix builds a diagnostic suffix for user-facing output
642	// when we fall through to the default "failed to generate the summary" path.
643	// Prefers the envelope Message, falls back to HTTP status, then exit code,
644	// so the user never sees a bare "Claude failed to generate the summary:"
645	// with nothing after the colon (which happens when Claude returns
646	// is_error:true with result:null, or when the subprocess crashes with no
647	// stderr output). ExitCode < 0 means the subprocess did not produce a real
648	// exit code (e.g. launch failure) — render that as "abnormal termination"
649	// rather than the misleading "exited with code -1".
650	func formatClaudeErrorSuffix(e *claudecode.ClaudeError) string {
651		if e.Message != "" {
652			return ": " + e.Message
653		}
654		switch {
655		case e.APIStatus != 0:
656			return fmt.Sprintf(" (Anthropic API returned HTTP %d)", e.APIStatus)
657		case e.ExitCode > 0:
658			return fmt.Sprintf(" (claude CLI exited with code %d)", e.ExitCode)
659		case e.ExitCode < 0:
660			return " (claude CLI terminated abnormally — no exit code captured)"
661		default:
662			return " (no diagnostic detail available from Claude CLI)"
663		}
664	}
665	
666	func formatSummaryTimeout(d time.Duration) string {
667		if d < 0 {
668			d = 0
669		}
670		if d < time.Second {
671			return d.Round(10 * time.Millisecond).String()
672		}
673		return d.Round(time.Second).String()
674	}

676	// explainTemporaryCheckpoint finds and formats a temporary checkpoint by shadow commit hash prefix.
677	// Returns the formatted output and whether the checkpoint was found.
678	// Searches ALL shadow branches, not just the one for current HEAD, to find checkpoints
679	// created from different base commits (e.g., if HEAD advanced since session start).
680	// The writer w is used for raw transcript output to bypass the pager.
681	func explainTemporaryCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, repo *git.Repository, store *checkpoint.GitStore, shaPrefix string, verbose, full, rawTranscript bool) (string, bool) {
682		// List temporary checkpoints from ALL shadow branches
683		// This ensures we find checkpoints even if HEAD has advanced since the session started
684		tempCheckpoints, err := store.ListAllTemporaryCheckpoints(ctx, "", branchCheckpointsLimit)
685		if err != nil {
686			return "", false
687		}
688	
689		// Find checkpoints matching the SHA prefix - check for ambiguity
690		var matches []checkpoint.TemporaryCheckpointInfo
691		for _, tc := range tempCheckpoints {
692			if strings.HasPrefix(tc.CommitHash.String(), shaPrefix) {
693				matches = append(matches, tc)
694			}
695		}
696	
697		if len(matches) == 0 {
698			return "", false
699		}

1	package claudecode
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6	)
7	
8	// ClaudeErrorKind classifies a typed Claude CLI error so callers can
9	// produce actionable user-facing messages without parsing strings.
10	type ClaudeErrorKind string
11	
12	const (
13		// ClaudeErrorAuth indicates an authentication or authorization failure
14		// (HTTP 401/403 in the CLI envelope, or recognized stderr substring).
15		ClaudeErrorAuth ClaudeErrorKind = "auth"
16		// ClaudeErrorRateLimit indicates the request was rejected for rate-limit
17		// or quota reasons (HTTP 429).
18		ClaudeErrorRateLimit ClaudeErrorKind = "rate_limit"
19		// ClaudeErrorConfig indicates a client-side request error other than
20		// auth or rate-limit (e.g., HTTP 4xx for invalid model or malformed args).
21		ClaudeErrorConfig ClaudeErrorKind = "config"
22		// ClaudeErrorCLIMissing indicates the claude binary was not found on PATH.
23		ClaudeErrorCLIMissing ClaudeErrorKind = "cli_missing"
24		// ClaudeErrorUnknown is the catch-all for failures we cannot classify.
25		ClaudeErrorUnknown ClaudeErrorKind = "unknown"
26	)
27	
28	// ClaudeError is a typed error returned by ClaudeCodeAgent's text generation
29	// methods. APIStatus and ExitCode use zero to mean "not applicable."
30	type ClaudeError struct {
31		Kind      ClaudeErrorKind
32		Message   string // user-safe text extracted from the CLI envelope or stderr
33		APIStatus int
34		ExitCode  int
35		Cause     error
36	}
37	
38	func (e *ClaudeError) Error() string {
39		if e.Message == "" {
40			if e.ExitCode != 0 {
41				return fmt.Sprintf("claude CLI error (kind=%s, exit=%d)", e.Kind, e.ExitCode)
42			}
43			return fmt.Sprintf("claude CLI error (kind=%s)", e.Kind)
44		}
45		return fmt.Sprintf("claude CLI error (kind=%s): %s", e.Kind, e.Message)
46	}
47	
48	func (e *ClaudeError) Unwrap() error { return e.Cause }
49	
50	const stderrMessageMaxLen = 500
51	
52	// authStderrPhrases is intentionally small. The primary auth-detection path
53	// is the structured envelope (classifyEnvelopeError); these phrases are a
54	// best-effort fallback for crashes that exit non-zero before the envelope
55	// is produced.
56	var authStderrPhrases = []string{
57		"invalid api key",
58		"not logged in",
59	}
60	
61	// classifyEnvelopeError converts a Claude CLI is_error:true envelope into a
62	// typed ClaudeError. The result text is treated as user-safe (the CLI
63	// produces it for human consumption).
64	func classifyEnvelopeError(resultText string, apiStatus *int, exitCode int) *ClaudeError {
65		e := &ClaudeError{
66			Message:  resultText,
67			ExitCode: exitCode,
68		}
69		if apiStatus != nil {
70			e.APIStatus = *apiStatus
71		}
72		switch {
73		case e.APIStatus == 401, e.APIStatus == 403:
74			e.Kind = ClaudeErrorAuth
75		case e.APIStatus == 429:
76			e.Kind = ClaudeErrorRateLimit
77		case e.APIStatus >= 400 && e.APIStatus < 500:
78			e.Kind = ClaudeErrorConfig
79		case e.APIStatus == 0 && hasAuthPhrase(resultText):
80			// No structured status (older CLI builds / internal errors) — fall
81			// back to the same phrase heuristic the stderr path uses so users
82			// still get auth-specific guidance.
83			e.Kind = ClaudeErrorAuth
84		default:
85			e.Kind = ClaudeErrorUnknown
86		}
87		return e
88	}
89	
90	// classifyStderrError is a fallback classifier used when the subprocess exited
91	// non-zero without producing a parseable envelope. It only attempts to
92	// recognize a small, stable set of auth phrases; everything else becomes
93	// ClaudeErrorUnknown with the (truncated) stderr as the message.
94	func classifyStderrError(stderr string, exitCode int) *ClaudeError {
95		msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr)
96		if len(msg) > stderrMessageMaxLen {
97			msg = msg[:stderrMessageMaxLen]
98		}
99		e := &ClaudeError{Message: msg, ExitCode: exitCode}
100		if hasAuthPhrase(msg) {
101			e.Kind = ClaudeErrorAuth
102			return e
103		}
104		e.Kind = ClaudeErrorUnknown
105		return e
106	}
107	
108	func hasAuthPhrase(s string) bool {
109		lower := strings.ToLower(s)
110		for _, phrase := range authStderrPhrases {
111			if strings.Contains(lower, phrase) {
112				return true
113			}
114		}
115		return false
116	}

# PR #963 Review — `feat: classify Claude CLI errors into actionable user messages`

## Overview
Replaces opaque `failed to parse summary JSON` errors with typed `*claudecode.ClaudeError` (Auth / RateLimit / Config / CLIMissing / Unknown). Wires `errors.As` from `claudecode.GenerateText` → `summarize.Generate` → `explain.formatCheckpointSummaryError`. Adds settings groundwork (`summary_timeout_seconds`) used by stacked follow-up. +866 / −37 with strong test coverage.

Direction is correct. Comments + negative-assertion tests are unusually disciplined.

## Findings

### Real concerns

- **`error.go:38-46` vs `explain.go:650-664` render `ExitCode<0` differently.** `Error()` prints `kind=unknown, exit=-1`. `formatClaudeErrorSuffix` renders the same condition as `"abnormal termination — no exit code captured"`. The latter is the intended UX (covered by `TestFormatCheckpointSummaryError_Unknown`); the former leaks through anywhere callers log `err.Error()` directly. Recommend `Error()` mirror the same `<0 → "abnormal"` rule, or share one helper.

- **`classifyStderrError` truncates *before* phrase match** (`error.go:95-100`). If `"Invalid API key"` appears past byte 500, classification falls through to `Unknown`. Match phrase first, then truncate the stored `Message`.

- **No test for envelope-is-error + non-zero exit** (`generate.go:58-69`). `TestGenerateText_EnvelopeErrorReturnsClaudeError` runs `printf` (exit 0). The branch that captures `exitErr.ExitCode()` on the envelope-error path is unexercised — exactly the OOM/SIGKILL-with-partial-stdout scenario this PR cites.

- **`summary_timeout_seconds` shipped without effect.** Settings field + accessor + test merge today, generate path doesn't read it (PR description acknowledges). Risk: users set it after release and report "summary_timeout_seconds is ignored." Either gate behind the follow-up PR or document as a no-op in the field comment + CHANGELOG.

### Minor

- **`generate.go:72-77` ctx checks discard `err`.** When `ctx.Err()` is non-nil for any reason (parent timeout, sibling cancel) we return the bare sentinel and drop `cmd.Run()`'s actual error (e.g., `fork: resource unavailable`). Comment acknowledges the trade-off; consider attaching `err` via `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` to the sentinel for log-side debuggability without changing user-facing routing (since `errors.Is` still matches).

- **`explain.go:626` default branch double-wraps.** `failed to generate summary: %w` over a now-rare unclassified error. Harmless but redundant — the inner error already begins with that phrase in many call sites. Worth a glance.

- **Stale Cursor bot comments.** Several existing PR comments reference symbols not in this diff (`GenerationProgress`, `summaryProgressWriter`, `TTFTms`, idle watchdog). Those belong to a stacked/different PR — confirm before resolving them on this one.

### Nits

- `error.go:79` envelope branch uses `e.APIStatus == 0 && hasAuthPhrase(...)` — same heuristic as stderr fallback. Could share via a single private helper to keep auth-detection in one place.
- `claude_test.go:59` shell-quoting JSON inside `printf` is fragile if a future test adds a single quote. Use a heredoc-style fixture or write a temp script.

## Risk
Medium — touches the `explain --generate` critical path. Mitigated by the regression tests that pin `errors.As` survival across both `summarize` layers (`TestGenerateFromTranscript_PreservesClaudeError`) and the bare-colon negative assertions. No security implications. No perf concerns.

## Verdict
Approve after addressing the `ExitCode<0` render inconsistency and the truncate-before-match ordering. Other items can be follow-ups.

[P2] Preserve stdout/exec detail for non-envelope Claude failures — /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/generate.go:81-86
    When cmd.Run() fails and stdout does not contain a parseable is_error envelope, this branch now classifies the failure from stderr alone. The previous helper
    fell back to stdout and finally err.Error(), so cases like a broken/incompatible claude binary or a non-zero exit that reports its error on stdout now collapse
    into ClaudeErrorUnknown with an empty message, and entire explain --generate ends up telling the user there is “no diagnostic detail”. Please keep stdout and
    the original exec error as fallbacks here so these failures stay actionable.
Will fix. Plan: at exec-failure path, prefer stderr → stdout → err.Error() so message non-empty + auth-phrase check still scans whichever source had detail.
